name: IFS
description: IFS checks multiple conditions and returns the value for the first condition that is true.
tldr: A simpler way to write multiple IF statements without nesting.

parameters.name: value_if_true1
parameters.description: The value to return if logical_test1 is true.

basicExample.description: Assign a grade based on a score
basicExample.explanation: Returns the first grade where the condition is true. If A2 is 85, returns "B".

advancedExamples.title: Nested conditions with default
advancedExamples.description: Return a commission rate with a fallback
advancedExamples.explanation: The TRUE condition at the end catches any remaining cases, acting as a default.

howItWorks: IFS evaluates each logical test from left to right. As soon as a test is true, it returns the corresponding value. If no test is true and no default TRUE condition is provided, it returns #N/A.

howToSteps.name: Write first condition
howToSteps.text: Enter the first logical test and its return value.

howToSteps.name: Add default if needed
howToSteps.text: Use TRUE as the last condition to return a default value.

limitations: Requires Excel 2019 or Excel 365; not available in older versions.
No explicit value_if_false argument; use a default TRUE condition.
Stops at the first true condition.

commonErrors.cause: No condition is true and no default condition is provided.
commonErrors.fix: Add TRUE, "default value" as the last pair.

commonErrors.cause: A logical test does not evaluate to TRUE/FALSE.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: IFS works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between IF and IFS?
faq.answer: IF handles one condition. IFS handles multiple conditions in a flat list without nesting.

faq.question: Can I use IFS in Excel 2016?
faq.answer: No, IFS requires Excel 2019 or Excel 365 or later.

faq.question: How do I add a default value in IFS?
faq.answer: Use TRUE as the final condition: IFS(..., TRUE, "default").
